newsitem.title: INDIA: India Reliance commissions new plant.
newsitem.headline: India Reliance commissions new plant.

text.p: India's largest private sector firm, Reliance Industries, said on Monday it had commissioned a polyethylene plant with a 200,000-tonne-per-year capacity at Hazira in the western state of Gujarat.
Reliance said the plant would reduce India's dependence on imported polyethylene to feed its plastics industry.
"With this (the new plant) RIL's polyethylene (PE) production has nearly doubled to 400,000 tonnes per year, placing it amongst the top ten global producers of PE," Reliance said in a statement.

Reliance's Hazira Petrochemicals Complex will now be able to produce the entire range of HDPE (high-density polyethylene) and LLDPE (low lipid density polyethylene) grades required by India's plastics processing industry, the statement added.

"The demand for polyethylene in India during the financial year 1996-97 was about 645,000 tonnes," the firm said. "At present nearly 45 percent of the demand is met through imports which will now be met by RIL's second PE plant."

Reliance estimated that the new plant's output would boost its market share to over 50 percent. But it stressed that India would continue to remain a net importer of PE until well into the next century.
"The demand in 1997-98 is expected to be about 750,000 tonnes," the statement added.
